Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

surprisingly adverb

also surprising, amazingly, astonishingly, remarkably, unexpectedly, to everyone’s surprise, it’s amazing how

classical

Caes. B.G. 1.41: mīrum in modum conversae sunt omnium mentēs (Lewis & Short, s.v. mīrus)

mīrum in modum

phrase

surprisingly, astonishingly

Literally “in a wonderful way”; it goes with a verb or an adjective. The comic poets have mīrīs modīs (Plaut., Ter.).

Other words

  • mīrum quam (quantum) — it’s amazing how (much)

    phrase · also used · classical · Liv. 2.1: id mīrum quantum prōfuit ad concordiam cīvitātis (Lewis & Short)

    Used as a single adverb, with the indicative: mīrum quantum “surprisingly much”.

  • praeter opīniōnem — unexpectedly, contrary to expectation

    phrase · also used · classical · Nep. Milt. 2.5: etsī praeter opīniōnem rēs ceciderat (Lewis & Short, s.v. opīniō); Cic. de Or. 2.284: praeter exspectātiōnem (Lewis & Short)

    When the surprise is that things went against what was expected; also contrā opīniōnem and praeter exspectātiōnem. With a comparative, opīniōne alone: opīniōne citius, “sooner than expected” (Varro) (see surprise-unexpected-thing).

Examples

  • id mīrum quantum prōfuit ad concordiam cīvitātis

    it did surprisingly much for harmony in the stateLiv. 2.1 (Lewis & Short)

  • Mīrum in modum crēvit puer.

    The boy has grown amazingly.composed

See also be surprised, surprise, strange.

SourcesLewis & Short: mirus · Lewis & Short: opinio · Lewis & Short: exspectatio
